questions.title: ATM Cashout Safety Gate
questions.description:
An ATM refuses withdrawals larger than the balance by raising ValueError("Insufficient funds") and catching it to print the message.
Read the balance and the requested amount.

Input Format:
Line 1: balance (integer)
Line 2: amount (integer)

Output Format:
Either: Dispensed <amount>
Or exactly: Insufficient funds

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 100000, 0 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Simulator
questions.description:
An ATM processes one withdrawal request against an account and reports the FIRST rule that fails, in this priority order:

1. The amount is more than the balance: print "Insufficient Balance".
2. The amount is not a multiple of 100: print "Invalid Amount".
3. The amount exceeds the daily limit of 10000: print "Daily Limit Exceeded".
4. Otherwise the withdrawal succeeds: print "Withdrawn. Remaining: X" where X is the new balance.

Combine the checks with an elif ladder (no and-chains) so the priority order is preserved.

Input Format:
Line 1: account balance (integer).
Line 2: withdrawal amount (integer).

Output Format:
One line with the result as described above.

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 100000, 1 <= amount <= 50000

questions.title: Access Log IP Tally
questions.description:
A security analyst mines a mini access log. Each line starts with an IPv4-style address; extract the address with a regex (no splitting), tally hits per address in a dictionary, then print every address with its count, sorted lexicographically by the address string.

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer n, the number of log lines
Lines 2 to n+1: each line starts with an IPv4-style address like 10.0.0.5 followed by request details; no other dotted quad appears in any line

Output Format:
One line per distinct address, sorted lexicographically as strings: <address> <count>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12; each address has four dot-separated groups of 1 to 3 digits.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 12, IPv4-style addresses with four groups of 1-3 digits

questions.title: Age In Days Engine
questions.description:
A government form service converts a birth date into an exact age measured against a reference date, reporting the total day count and its breakdown into full weeks and leftover days using timedelta arithmetic.

Input Format:
Line 1: birth date as DD-MM-YYYY
Line 2: reference date as DD-MM-YYYY (same day or later)

Output Format:
Line 1: Days: <total days between the two dates>
Line 2: Weeks: <total // 7>, Days: <total % 7>

Constraints:
Both dates are valid calendar dates between 1900-01-01 and 2100-12-31; the total is at most 73000 days.
questions.inputconstrains: reference date >= birth date, total <= 73000 days
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

birth = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
ref = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
span = ref - birth
total = span.days
print(f"Days: {total}")
rest = span - timedelta(weeks=total // 7)
print(f"Weeks: {total // 7}, Days: {rest.days}")

questions.title: Allergy-Safe Kiosk
questions.description:
A food kiosk checks every dish on its menu against a customer's allergy set. A dish is safe only when it shares NO ingredient with the allergies — decide this with the set intersection method and print the safe menu.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: dish name, then integer k, then k ingredient names — all separated by spaces. Next line: integer m. Last line: m allergy names separated by spaces.

Output Format:
One line per safe dish, in menu order. Last line: Total safe: k

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 30; each dish has 1..6 ingredients; 1..8 allergies; all names are lowercase single words of up to 15 characters.
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
dishes = []
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split()
    name = parts[0]
    ingredients = set(parts[2:])
    dishes.append((name, ingredients))
m = int(input())
allergies = set(input().split())
safe_count = 0
for name, ingredients in dishes:
    if len(ingredients.intersection(allergies)) == 0:
        print(name)
        safe_count += 1
print("Total safe:", safe_count)

questions.title: Analytics Grid Dashboard
questions.description:
A metrics dashboard renders a numeric grid entirely with comprehensions: row totals, column totals and the grand total. Build every aggregate with comprehensions only - no .append, no map, no filter. Row totals come from one comprehension over the rows; column totals from a nested comprehension that walks each column index.

Input Format:
Line 1: r and c separated by a space.
Lines 2..r+1: each row with c integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the r row totals, space separated.
Line 2: the c column totals, space separated.
Line 3: the grand total.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 10, -100 <= value <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
r, c = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
grid = [[int(x) for x in input().split()] for _ in range(r)]
row_sums = [sum(row) for row in grid]
col_sums = [sum(grid[i][j] for i in range(r)) for j in range(c)]
print(" ".join(str(s) for s in row_sums))
print(" ".join(str(s) for s in col_sums))
print(sum(row_sums))

questions.title: Appointment Slot Conflict Check
questions.description:
A clinic scheduler stores two appointment slots written as full timestamps. Decide whether the slots overlap: they clash when slot 1 starts before slot 2 ends AND slot 2 starts before slot 1 ends. Slots that merely touch at an endpoint do not overlap.

Input Format:
Four lines, each DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM: slot 1 start, slot 1 end, slot 2 start, slot 2 end (all four share one date; each slot's end is after its start).

Output Format:
One line: Overlap or No overlap

Constraints:

questions.inputconstrains: four timestamps share one date, each slot end after its start
questions.sourcecode:
from datetime import datetime

s1 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
e1 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
s2 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")
e2 = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y %H:%M")

questions.title: Asset Pipeline Manifest Audit
questions.description:
A release pipeline audits its manifest. Read the base folder and then n asset names. questions.title: Async ETL Validation
questions.description:
An ETL job processes incoming records through two chained async stages. Read k records (an id and a raw value token each). Stage 1 (async validate): the record is VALID only if the value token parses as an integer AND 0 <= value <= 1000. Stage 2 (async transform): valid values are doubled. In async main, walk the records in order, awaiting validate and then transform, count valid and invalid records, collect the transformed values in input order, then print: line 1 the transformed values space-separated (or none if there are no valid records), line 2 valid=X invalid=Y.

Input Format:
Line 1: k
Next k lines: record_id value (space separated).

Output Format:
Line 1: transformed values space-separated, or the word none
Line 2: valid=X invalid=Y

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 20; value is an integer token or a non-numeric token
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= k <= 20; value is an integer token or a non-numeric token
questions.sourcecode:
import asyncio

k = int(input())
records = []
for _ in range(k):
    parts = input().split()
    records.append((parts[0], parts[1]))

async def validate(raw):
    try:
        v = int(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if v < 0 or v > 1000:
        return None
    return v

async def transform(v):
    return v * 2

async def main():
    valid = 0
    invalid = 0
    out = []
    for rec_id, raw in records:
        v = await validate(raw)
        if v is None:
            invalid += 1
        else:
            t = await transform(v)
            out.append(str(t))
            valid += 1
    if out:
        print(" ".join(out))
    else:
        print("none")
    print("valid=" + str(valid) + " invalid=" + str(invalid))

asyncio.run(main())

questions.title: Async Health Checker
questions.description:
A microservice dashboard probes two services with async stub handlers. Read each service's name and its simulated latency in milliseconds. Define an async probe(name, ms) that returns the string name:NNms. In async main, await probe for service 1, then for service 2, printing each result line in input order.

Input Format:
Line 1: service1_name ms1
Line 2: service2_name ms2

Output Format:
Line 1: name1:ms1ms
Line 2: name2:ms2ms

Constraints:
Names are single tokens; 1 <= ms <= 2000
questions.sourcecode:
import asyncio

name1, ms1 = input().split()
name2, ms2 = input().split()
ms1 = int(ms1)
ms2 = int(ms2)

async def probe(name, ms):
    return name + ":" + str(ms) + "ms"

async def main():
    r1 = await probe(name1, ms1)
    r2 = await probe(name2, ms2)
    print(r1)
    print(r2)

asyncio.run(main())

questions.title: Audit Chain Appends
questions.description:
A compliance tool builds an audit trail: a header line is written once, then events are appended across two separate append sessions. Read n events. Open /tmp/atom_audit.txt with mode w and write the header audit start. Then append the first half of the events (one open/append/close session per event), and afterwards append the second half in a second session. Finally read the whole file and print every line in order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: event text.

Output Format:
The full audit chain: audit start, then all n events in order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 8; each line 1 <= L <= 40
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
events = []
for _ in range(n):
    events.append(input())
half = (n + 1) // 2

w = open("/tmp/atom_audit.txt", "w")
w.write("audit start\n")
w.close()

for e in events[:half]:
    a = open("/tmp/atom_audit.txt", "a")
    a.write(e + "\n")
    a.close()

for e in events[half:]:
    a = open("/tmp/atom_audit.txt", "a")
    a.write(e + "\n")
    a.close()

r = open("/tmp/atom_audit.txt", "r")
print(r.read(), end="")
r.close()

questions.title: Backup Copier Count
questions.description:
A tiny backup tool copies one file to another using two with-open handles in a single statement. Read n lines, write them into /tmp/atom_source.txt, then open BOTH /tmp/atom_source.txt (read) and /tmp/atom_backup.txt (write) with one with statement and copy the content line by line. Print how many lines were copied.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: the source text lines.

Output Format:
One line: the number of copied lines.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10; each line 1 <= L <= 60

n = int(input())
lines = []
for _ in range(n):
    lines.append(input())
with open("/tmp/atom_source.txt", "w") as f:
    for line in lines:
        f.write(line + "\n")
copied = 0
with open("/tmp/atom_source.txt", "r") as src, open("/tmp/atom_backup.txt", "w") as dst:
    for line in src:
        dst.write(line)
        copied += 1
print(copied)

questions.title: Bakery Batch Cost Tracker
questions.description:
A bakery logs every batch it bakes with the item name, how many pieces were made and the price per piece.
Write a class Batch whose constructor stores the item name, the quantity and the unit price, and a method total_cost() that returns quantity * unit_price.

Line 2: quantity and unit price (space separated, unit price may be fractional)

Output Format:
Print 'Batch <item>: <total>' with the total to exactly two decimal places.

0 <= quantity <= 1000 and 0 <= unit_price <= 5000
questions.sourcecode:
class Batch:
    def __init__(self, item, quantity, unit_price):
        self.item = item
        self.quantity = quantity
        self.unit_price = unit_price

    def total_cost(self):
        return self.quantity * self.unit_price

item = input()
quantity, unit_price = input().split()
b = Batch(item, int(quantity), float(unit_price))

questions.title: Bulk Order Discount Engine
questions.description:
A wholesaler prices bulk orders with a tier engine. Define order_total(*args) that aggregates any number of prices with a plain accumulation loop, and discount_rate(total) that maps the subtotal to a tier: 20 percent from 1000 up, 10 percent from 500 up to anything below 1000, otherwise none. Read the prices, call the aggregator by unpacking the list, and print the full quote. Input Format: Line 1: n. Line 2: n prices (floats). Output Format: 'Subtotal: ' (2 decimals), 'Discount: %' and 'Payable:

' (2 decimals). Constraints: 1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= price <= 100000
questions.sourcecode:
def order_total(*args):
    total = 0
    for p in args:
        total += p
    return total

def discount_rate(total):
    if total >= 1000:
        return 20
    if total >= 500:
        return 10
    return 0

n = int(input())
prices = list(map(float, input().split()))
subtotal = order_total(*prices)
rate = discount_rate(subtotal)
discount = subtotal * rate / 100
payable = subtotal - discount
print(f"Subtotal: {subtotal:.2f}")
print(f"Discount: {rate}%")
print(f"Payable: {payable:.2f}")

questions.title: Certificate Template Engine
questions.description:
An academy's certificate generator fills placeholder tokens written as {key} inside a template line.
The string-method toolbox on the print server is broken, so fill the template by scanning it character by character: when a { starts a token, read until } and substitute the mapped value.
Every token in the template has a mapping.

Input Format:
Line 1: the template line (may contain {key} placeholders)
Line 2: n, the number of mappings
Next n lines: key value (the value is a single token without spaces)

Output Format:
The filled template line.

Constraints:
1 <= len(template) <= 300, 1 <= n <= 10, tokens are well-formed {key} with no nesting
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(template) <= 300, 1 <= n <= 10, values have no spaces
questions.sourcecode:
template = input()
n = int(input())
values = {}
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split()
    values[parts[0]] = parts[1]
out = []
i = 0
while i < len(template):
    ch = template[i]
    if ch == "{":
        j = template.find("}", i)
        key = template[i + 1:j]
        out.append(values[key])
        i = j + 1
    else:
        out.append(ch)
        i += 1
print("".join(out))

import asyncio

weights_b = [int(x) for x in input().split()]

async def deliver(weights):
    total = 0
    count = 0

        count += 1
    return total, count

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

NAMES = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]

def main():
    a = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
    b = datetime.strptime(input(), "%d-%m-%Y")
    ends = 0
    cur = a
    while cur <= b:
        nxt = cur + timedelta(days=1)
        mark = ""
        if nxt.day == 1:
            mark = " [Month end]"
            ends += 1
        print(f"{cur.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')} {NAMES[cur.weekday()]}{mark}")
        cur = nxt
    print(f"Month ends: {ends}")

main()

questions.description:
A branch ledger is shared by a deposit teller and a withdrawal teller, both updating one balance under a single lock. Read the starting balance, the number of unit-deposits, and the number of unit-withdrawals. Each teller thread applies its operations one at a time while holding the lock, and every lock acquisition counts as one operation. Join both tellers, then print the final balance and the total number of lock operations (deposits + withdrawals).

One line: balance dep wdr

Output Format:

Line 2: total lock operations

import threading

balance, dep, wdr = map(int, input().split())
lock = threading.Lock()
ops = 0

def apply_deposits(n):
    global balance, ops
    for _ in range(n):
        with lock:
            balance += 1
            ops += 1

def apply_withdrawals(n):
    global balance, ops
    for _ in range(n):
        with lock:
            balance -= 1
            ops += 1

t1 = threading.Thread(target=apply_deposits, args=(dep,))
t2 = threading.Thread(target=apply_withdrawals, args=(wdr,))
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()
print(balance)
print(ops)

    n = int(input())
    best_eff = -1.0
    best_name = ""
    eff_total = 0.0
    dist_total = 0.0
    fuel_total = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        parts = input().split()
        name = parts[0]
        dist = float(parts[1])
        fuel = float(parts[2])
        eff = dist / fuel
        eff_total = eff_total + eff
        dist_total = dist_total + dist
        fuel_total = fuel_total + fuel
        print(f"{name}: {eff:.2f} km/L")
        if eff > best_eff:
            best_eff = eff
            best_name = name
    print(f"Best: {best_name} ({best_eff:.2f} km/L)")
    print(f"Avg: {eff_total / n:.2f} km/L")
    print(f"Fleet distance: {dist_total:.2f} km")
    print(f"Fleet fuel used: {fuel_total:.2f} L")

main()

questions.title: Grade Ledger Default Trap
questions.description:
A coaching tracker keeps one shared ledger. Define record(score, ledger=[]) that appends the score to its ledger argument, totals the ledger with a plain loop, and returns (count, total, average); define verdict(average) returning 'On track' when the average is at least 40, else 'Needs work'. Read m scores, calling record without a ledger argument each time, and print the running analytics after every call — watch how the default list remembers across calls.

Input Format:

Output Format:

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 20; 0 <= score <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
def record(score, ledger=[]):
    ledger.append(score)
    total = 0
    for s in ledger:
        total += s
    count = len(ledger)
    average = total / count
    return count, total, average

def verdict(average):
    if average < 40:
        return "Needs work"
    return "On track"

m = int(input())
for _ in range(m):
    score = int(input())
    count, total, average = record(score)
    print(f"Call {count}: total {total} average {average:.2f} ({verdict(average)})")

questions.description:
An exam control room assigns hall seat numbers from one class-level counter, so every seat created anywhere shares a single sequence starting at 1. The hall has a capacity; applicants who arrive after the hall is full are rejected.
Write a class ExamSeat with a class attribute next_number set to 1. Its constructor stores the student name, takes the current counter value as the seat number, and then advances the shared counter by 1. Write a class Hall whose constructor stores the capacity and an empty seat list; its method seat(student) creates an ExamSeat while the hall is below capacity and returns '<student>: seat <number>', otherwise returns '<student>: HALL FULL'.

Input Format:
Line 1: capacity and number of applicants n (space separated)
Next n lines: one student name each

Output Format:
One line per applicant in arrival order.
Then 'Assigned: <count>' and 'Next seat: <ExamSeat.next_number>'.

Constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 100, 1 <= n <= 200 and 1 <= len(name) <= 20
questions.sourcecode:
class ExamSeat:
    next_number = 1

    def __init__(self, student):
        self.student = student
        self.seat_no = ExamSeat.next_number
        ExamSeat.next_number += 1

class Hall:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.seats = []

    def seat(self, student):
        if len(self.seats) < self.capacity:
            s = ExamSeat(student)
            self.seats.append(s)
            return f"{student}: seat {s.seat_no}"
        return f"{student}: HALL FULL"

capacity, n = input().split()
hall = Hall(int(capacity))
n = int(n)
for _ in range(n):
    name = input()
    print(hall.seat(name))
print(f"Assigned: {len(hall.seats)}")
print(f"Next seat: {ExamSeat.next_number}")

questions.title: Lock-Guarded Click Counter
questions.description:
Drill: a shared counter incremented by two threads under a threading.Lock. Read two integers k1 and k2. Thread A increments a global counter k1 times and thread B increments it k2 times, every increment performed while holding the lock. Join both threads, then print the final counter value.

Output Format:

Constraints:
0 <= k1, k2 <= 200

import threading

k1, k2 = map(int, input().split())
count = 0
lock = threading.Lock()

def clicker(n):
    global count
    for _ in range(n):
        with lock:
            count += 1

t1 = threading.Thread(target=clicker, args=(k1,))
t2 = threading.Thread(target=clicker, args=(k2,))
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()
print(count)

questions.title: Log Rotation Archiver
questions.description:
A syslog-style service rotates its log: only the newest k lines stay in the main file, everything older moves to an archive file. Read n log lines and k. Write all lines to /tmp/atom_main_log.txt, read the file back by iterating the file object (no readlines), then rewrite the main file with only the LAST k lines and write the moved lines into /tmp/atom_archive.txt. Print: archived=A (lines moved), kept=K (lines remaining in the main file, counted by reading it back), then the archive content, one line per line (nothing extra if the archive is empty).

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: log lines.
Last line: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:
Line 1: archived=A
Line 2: kept=K
Then the archived lines in order (if any).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12; 1 <= k <= n; each line 1 <= L <= 20
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
logs = []
for _ in range(n):
    logs.append(input())
k = int(input())

with open("/tmp/atom_main_log.txt", "w") as f:
    for line in logs:
        f.write(line + "\n")

all_lines = []
with open("/tmp/atom_main_log.txt", "r") as f:
    for line in f:
        all_lines.append(line.rstrip("\n"))

if k < len(all_lines):
    archive_lines = all_lines[:len(all_lines) - k]
    keep_lines = all_lines[len(all_lines) - k:]
else:
    archive_lines = []
    keep_lines = all_lines

with open("/tmp/atom_main_log.txt", "w") as f:
    for line in keep_lines:
        f.write(line + "\n")
with open("/tmp/atom_archive.txt", "w") as f:
    for line in archive_lines:
        f.write(line + "\n")

kept = 0
with open("/tmp/atom_main_log.txt", "r") as f:
    for line in f:
        kept += 1
print("archived=" + str(len(archive_lines)))
print("kept=" + str(kept))
with open("/tmp/atom_archive.txt", "r") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.rstrip("\n"))

questions.description:
An industrial controller watches four safety sensors, each reporting 0 (triggered/false) or 1 (clear/true). From the sensor booleans a, b, c, d it evaluates three expressions exactly as Python does (not binds tighter than and, which binds tighter than or):

r1 = not a and b or not c and d        (read as ((not a) and b) or ((not c) and d))
r2 = not (a and b) or not (c and d)
r3 = (not a or b) and (not c or d)

Print r1, r2, r3, then how many of them are True, then "SAFE" if at least 2 are True else "INSPECT".

Input Format:
One line with four space-separated values a b c d, each 0 or 1.

Output Format:
Five lines: r1, r2, r3 (each True or False), the count of True results (0-3), then SAFE or INSPECT.

Constraints:
Each of a, b, c, d is 0 or 1.
questions.inputconstrains: each of a b c d is 0 or 1
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    a, b, c, d = [v == "1" for v in input().split()]
    r1 = (not a and b) or (not c and d)
    r2 = not (a and b) or not (c and d)
    r3 = (not a or b) and (not c or d)
    count = (1 if r1 else 0) + (1 if r2 else 0) + (1 if r3 else 0)
    print(r1)
    print(r2)
    print(r3)
    print(count)
    print("SAFE" if count >= 2 else "INSPECT")


main()

questions.title: Lucky Draw Session Audit
questions.description:
Your game studio runs a deterministic lucky-draw simulator to balance loot tables. It seeds Python's random module with a fixed seed, draws k integers in the range 1..100 with random.randint, then audits the session.

Input Format:

Line 2: how many draws were greater than or equal to threshold.
Line 3: the highest drawn number.
Line 4: how many distinct values were drawn.

import random

seed, k, threshold = map(int, input().split())
random.seed(seed)
draws = []
for _ in range(k):
    draws.append(random.randint(1, 100))

top = draws[0]
jackpots = 0
for d in draws:
    if d > top:
        top = d
    if d >= threshold:
        jackpots += 1

distinct = []
for d in draws:
    if d not in distinct:
        distinct.append(d)

print(" ".join(str(d) for d in draws))
print(jackpots)
print(top)
print(len(distinct))

questions.title: Multi-Counter Audit
questions.description:
A server farm keeps named event counters in one shared dictionary guarded by a single lock. Read n teller threads; each line names a counter key and how many times that thread bumps it. Each bump is one increment of that key performed while holding the lock. Join every thread, then print every counter key in sorted order as: key count, one per line, followed by a line: total N (sum of all counter values).

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: key times (space separated).

Output Format:
One line per key in sorted key order: key count
Final line: total N

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5; 0 <= times <= 50; keys are single tokens
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 5; 0 <= times <= 50; keys are single tokens
questions.sourcecode:
import threading

n = int(input())
counters = {}
lock = threading.Lock()

def bump(key, times):
    with lock:
        if key not in counters:
            counters[key] = 0
    for _ in range(times):
        with lock:
            counters[key] = counters[key] + 1

threads = []
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split()
    key = parts[0]
    times = int(parts[1])
    t = threading.Thread(target=bump, args=(key, times))
    threads.append(t)
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()

total = 0
for key in sorted(counters.keys()):
    print(key, counters[key])
    total = total + counters[key]
print("total", total)

questions.description:
A payroll system cuts salaries on the 10th and the 25th of each month. For a given month, report both cutoff dates with a weekend flag, then count the weekend days (Saturdays and Sundays) and the working days in the whole month.

Input Format:

Output Format:

from datetime import datetime
import calendar

def main():
    first = datetime.strptime(input(), "%m-%Y")
    y, m = first.year, first.month
    ndays = calendar.monthrange(y, m)[1]
    c1 = datetime(y, m, 10)
    c2 = datetime(y, m, 25)
    flag1 = "Weekend" if c1.weekday() >= 5 else "Working day"
    flag2 = "Weekend" if c2.weekday() >= 5 else "Working day"
    wknd = 0
    for dnum in range(1, ndays + 1):
        if datetime(y, m, dnum).weekday() >= 5:
            wknd += 1
    print(f"Cutoff 1: {c1.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')} {flag1}")
    print(f"Cutoff 2: {c2.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')} {flag2}")
    print(f"Weekend days: {wknd}")
    print(f"Working days: {ndays - wknd}")

main()

questions.title: Precedence Puzzle Solver
questions.description:
A maths worksheet generator evaluates the same four integers through three evaluation styles of one expression pattern, to teach operator precedence. Given a, b, c, d:

v1 = a + b * c ** 2 - d        (Python's real precedence: ** first, then *, then + and -)
v2 = ((a + b) * c) ** 2 - d    (strict left-to-right evaluation, ignoring precedence)
v3 = a + b * (c ** 2 - d)      (the c ** 2 - d part grouped first)

Print v1, v2 and v3, then the two differences v2 - v1 and v3 - v1. Do not use eval, max or min; compute each value explicitly with arithmetic operators.

Input Format:
One line with four space-separated integers a b c d.

Output Format:
Five lines, in this exact order: v1, v2, v3, v2 - v1, v3 - v1.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b, c, d <= 20
questions.sourcecode:
a, b, c, d = map(int, input().split())
v1 = a + b * c ** 2 - d
v2 = ((a + b) * c) ** 2 - d
v3 = a + b * (c ** 2 - d)
print(v1)
print(v2)
print(v3)
print(v2 - v1)
print(v3 - v1)

questions.title: Progressive Tax Engine
questions.description:
A tax authority computes yearly tax from income I (whole rupees) in slabs:

- up to 250000: no tax
- 250001 to 500000: 5% of the amount above 250000
- 500001 to 1000000: 12500 plus 10% of the amount above 500000
- above 1000000: 62500 plus 20% of the amount above 1000000

A surcharge of 10% of the tax applies only when the income is strictly greater than 1200000. Print the net payable amount (tax + surcharge) and the effective rate (net payable / income * 100), both with exactly 2 decimal places. Do not use elif; express every branch as chained conditional (ternary) expressions.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer income.

Output Format:
Two lines: net payable (2 decimals), then the effective rate (2 decimals).

Constraints:
1 <= income <= 10000000
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    i = int(input())
    tax = (
        0
        if i <= 250000
        else (i - 250000) * 0.05
        if i <= 500000
        else 12500 + (i - 500000) * 0.10
        if i <= 1000000
        else 62500 + (i - 1000000) * 0.20
    )
    sur = tax * 0.10 if i > 1200000 else 0
    net = tax + sur
    rate = net / i * 100
    print(f"{net:.2f}")
    print(f"{rate:.2f}")


main()

questions.title: Racing Standings Report
questions.description:
A racing team simulates lap timings per rider on its own thread (total time = laps * lap_time_ms, pure arithmetic). Read n riders: name, laps, and lap time in ms. Start one thread per rider which computes that rider's total into a slot. Join all riders. Then build the standings yourself WITHOUT any built-in sort: order riders by total time ascending (totals are guaranteed distinct) using your own comparison loop, and print rank lines: RANK. NAME TOTAL (rank starting at 1), followed by a line: winner NAME.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Next n lines: name laps lap_ms (space separated).

Output Format:
One line per rider, fastest first: RANK. NAME TOTAL
Final line: winner NAME

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 5; 1 <= laps <= 10; 1 <= lap_ms <= 1000; totals are distinct; names are single tokens
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= n <= 5; 1 <= laps <= 10; 1 <= lap_ms <= 1000; totals are distinct
questions.sourcecode:
import threading

n = int(input())
names = []
laps = []
lap_ms = []
for _ in range(n):
    parts = input().split()
    names.append(parts[0])
    laps.append(int(parts[1]))
    lap_ms.append(int(parts[2]))

totals = [0] * n

def ride(i):
    totals[i] = laps[i] * lap_ms[i]

threads = []
for i in range(n):
    t = threading.Thread(target=ride, args=(i,))
    threads.append(t)
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()

order = []
for i in range(n):
    order.append(i)
for a in range(n):
    for b in range(a + 1, n):
        if totals[order[b]] < totals[order[a]]:
            order[a], order[b] = order[b], order[a]

for rank in range(n):
    i = order[rank]
    print(str(rank + 1) + ". " + names[i] + " " + str(totals[i]))
print("winner " + names[order[0]])

questions.title: Readlines Count and Close
questions.description:
Drill: readlines() returns the list of all lines, and open files must be closed. Read n, then n lines. Write them all to /tmp/atom_rows.txt. Then open the file with mode r, call readlines(), store the result, and close() the handle explicitly. Print how many lines readlines() returned.

Next n lines: text lines.

Output Format:
One line: the number of lines in the file.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10; each line 1 <= L <= 60

n = int(input())
lines = []
for _ in range(n):
    lines.append(input())

for line in lines:

Output Format:
One line per run, in order: the character, a space, its count.

Constraints:
1 <= len(s) <= 1000, lowercase letters only

s = input().strip()
starts = [0] + [i for i in range(1, len(s)) if s[i] != s[i - 1]]

questions.title: Script Run Log Analyzer
questions.description:
A CI runner logs executions of Python practice scripts and needs a summary report.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Then n lines: STATUS NAME TIME where STATUS is OK or FAIL, NAME is a single-token script name and TIME is the run duration in seconds (a decimal number).

Output Format:
Line 1: Total runs: <n>
Line 2: Passed: <count of OK runs>
Line 3: Failed: <count of FAIL runs>
Line 4: Slowest: <name> (<time with 2 decimals>s) for the run with the largest TIME; if several runs tie, use the earliest one in the log.

1 <= n <= 20; 0.1 <= TIME <= 99.9.
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    n = int(input())
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    best_time = -1.0
    best_name = ""
    for i in range(n):
        parts = input().split()
        status = parts[0]
        name = parts[1]
        t = float(parts[2])
        if status == "OK":
            passed = passed + 1
        else:
            failed = failed + 1
        if t > best_time:
            best_time = t
            best_name = name
    print(f"Total runs: {n}")
    print(f"Passed: {passed}")
    print(f"Failed: {failed}")
    print(f"Slowest: {best_name} ({best_time:.2f}s)")

main()

questions.title: Sensor Byte Checksum Builder
questions.description:
An IoT gateway validates a batch of sensor readings. Given n bytes (each 0-255), build:

checksum: the bitwise XOR of all n bytes (start from 0 and XOR them in order).
alarm bytes: how many bytes have bit 7 (value 128) set.
frame word: the 16-bit frame (checksum << 8) | alarm_count.
status: "ALARM" if at least one alarm byte was seen, otherwise "CLEAR".

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of bytes.
Line 2: n space-separated integers (each 0-255).

Output Format:
Four lines, in this exact order: checksum, alarm byte count, frame word, status.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, each byte is between 0 and 255
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, each byte is between 0 and 255
questions.sourcecode:
def main():
    n = int(input())
    vals = list(map(int, input().split()))
    checksum = 0
    alarms = 0
    for b in vals:
        checksum ^= b
        if b & 128:
            alarms += 1
    frame = (checksum << 8) | alarms
    print(checksum)
    print(alarms)
    print(frame)
    print("ALARM" if alarms > 0 else "CLEAR")


main()

line_b = [int(x) for x in input().split()]

def poll(sensor_id, readings):
    best = readings[0]
    for r in readings:
        if r > best:

    peaks[sensor_id] = best

t2 = threading.Thread(target=poll, args=(1, line_b))

t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()

questions.title: Shard Sum Reduce
questions.description:
A log pipeline splits a day's events into shards. Read the number of shards n, then n lines of integers (one shard per line). Start one worker thread per shard; each thread sums its own shard and stores the result in its slot. Join all workers, then reduce: print every shard sum on its own line in shard order, followed by the grand total.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (number of shards)
Next n lines: space-separated integers for that shard.

Output Format:
n lines: each shard's sum in shard order, then one line with the grand total.

questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= n <= 4; each shard has 1 to 10 integers, 0 <= x <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
import threading

n = int(input())
shards = []
for _ in range(n):
    shards.append([int(x) for x in input().split()])
sums = [0] * n

def reduce_shard(idx):
    total = 0
    for v in shards[idx]:
        total += v
    sums[idx] = total

threads = []
for i in range(n):
    t = threading.Thread(target=reduce_shard, args=(i,))
    threads.append(t)
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()

grand = 0
for s in sums:
    grand += s
    print(s)
print(grand)

Drill: creating threads with result slots. Read two integers a and b. Start thread 1 which computes a*a and stores it into slot 0 of a shared results list, and thread 2 which computes b*b and stores it into slot 1. The threads print nothing; they only compute. Join both threads, then print slot 0 and slot 1.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b separated by a space.

Output Format:
Line 1: a*a
Line 2: b*b

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
import threading

a, b = map(int, input().split())
results = [0, 0]

def worker(idx, base):
    results[idx] = base * base

t1 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(0, a))
t2 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(1, b))
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()
print(results[0])
print(results[1])

questions.title: Three Worker Slots
questions.description:
Drill: the thread lifecycle — start then join. Read three integers v1 v2 v3. Start three threads; thread i (for i = 0, 1, 2) computes its value times 10 and records it into slots[i]. Threads print nothing. Join all three threads, then print the three slots separated by spaces.

Input Format:
One line with three integers v1 v2 v3 separated by spaces.

Output Format:
One line: the three slot values separated by spaces, in slot order.

Constraints:
3 values, each 0 <= v <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
import threading

values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
slots = [0, 0, 0]

def record(idx, v):
    slots[idx] = v * 10

threads = []
for i in range(3):
    t = threading.Thread(target=record, args=(i, values[i]))
    threads.append(t)
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()
print(slots[0], slots[1], slots[2])

questions.title: Ticket Pool Sell-Off
questions.description:
A stadium kiosk runs two seller threads that both draw from one shared ticket pool, guarded by a lock. Read the total tickets, how many seller A sells, and how many seller B sells. Each seller decrements the shared remaining count one ticket at a time under the lock. Join both sellers and print how many tickets remain.

Input Format:
One line: total sold_a sold_b

Output Format:
One line: remaining tickets.

Constraints:
0 <= sold_a + sold_b <= total <= 500
questions.sourcecode:
import threading

total, sold_a, sold_b = map(int, input().split())
remaining = total
lock = threading.Lock()

def sell(count):
    global remaining
    for _ in range(count):
        with lock:
            remaining -= 1

t1 = threading.Thread(target=sell, args=(sold_a,))
t2 = threading.Thread(target=sell, args=(sold_b,))
t1.start()
t2.start()
t1.join()
t2.join()
print(remaining)

questions.title: Transactional Journal Undo
questions.description:
A tiny journal supports full undo. The program starts each run with an empty journal file. Read m journal lines. Each line is either a transaction (any other text) or the marker ROLLBACK. Process lines in order: a transaction is APPENDED to /tmp/atom_journal.txt (append mode) and kept in memory; ROLLBACK performs a FULL undo — the in-memory list is cleared and the file is REWRITTEN from scratch (mode w) with the surviving content, which after a full undo is nothing. When all lines are processed, read the file back and print every surviving line in order.

Input Format:
Line 1: m
Next m lines: transaction text or the exact marker ROLLBACK.

Output Format:
The final journal content, one line per surviving transaction.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 12; entries 1..30 chars; at least one transaction survives the last ROLLBACK
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= m <= 12; entries 1..30 chars; one TX survives
questions.sourcecode:
m = int(input())
entries = []
for _ in range(m):
    entries.append(input())

path = "/tmp/atom_journal.txt"
live = []
with open(path, "w") as f:
    f.write("")
for entry in entries:
    if entry == "ROLLBACK":
        live = []
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            for e in live:
                f.write(e + "\n")
    else:
        live.append(entry)
        with open(path, "a") as f:
            f.write(entry + "\n")

with open(path, "r") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.rstrip("\n"))

questions.title: Tuple Ledger Reconciliation
questions.description:
A tiny accounting app stores ledgers as immutable tuples of (key, value) pairs. Ledger A and ledger B must be reconciled into ONE tuple ledger: start from A's entries in order, then process B's entries in order — if a key is already present, that entry's value is replaced in place; otherwise the new entry is appended at the end. Because tuples are immutable, every replacement and append must rebuild the tuple via concatenation (no dicts, no lists of records, no mutation).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: key and integer value separated by a space (ledger A, keys unique within A). Next line: integer m. Next m lines: key and integer value (ledger B, keys unique within B).

Output Format:
The reconciled ledger, one "key value" pair per line, in merged order.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 50; keys are single tokens of up to 15 characters; values in 0..1000; keys are unique within each ledger (they may overlap between ledgers).
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n, m <= 50, values in 0..1000, keys unique per ledger
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
ledger = ()
keys = ()
for _ in range(n):
    k, v = input().split()
    ledger = ledger + ((k, int(v)),)
    keys = keys + (k,)
m = int(input())
for _ in range(m):
    k, v = input().split()
    v = int(v)
    if k in keys:
        i = keys.index(k)
        ledger = ledger[:i] + ((k, v),) + ledger[i + 1:]
    else:
        ledger = ledger + ((k, v),)
        keys = keys + (k,)
for k, v in ledger:
    print(k, v)

Check the codeword manually with a two-pointer loop (compare the first and last characters while moving inward) - no slicing shortcuts.

Input Format:
One line: the codeword (lowercase letters)

Output Format:
Print "Palindrome" if it reads the same both ways, otherwise "Not Palindrome".

Constraints:
1 <= len(word) <= 100, lowercase letters only
questions.sourcecode:
word = input()
left = 0
right = len(word) - 1
is_pal = True
while left < right:
    if word[left] != word[right]:
        is_pal = False
        break
    left += 1
    right -= 1
if is_pal:
    print("Palindrome")
else:
    print("Not Palindrome")
